info.name: Mile Marker API
info.description:
Mile Marker API plans a fuel-efficient road trip between two US cities: the route, where to stop for fuel, and what it costs, with a GeoJSON map.
The one collection variable is base_url (default http://127.0.0.1:8000); change it to point at another server.
Run the requests in order: the Demo folder saves figures from the first request and the next three check themselves against them. The Errors folder and the Health and schema folder need no earlier request.
The collection's own script checks every 200 from the route: the walk along the stops, the cost of each stop and the map points. It also draws the map in the Visualize tab.
From the command line: npx newman run docs/postman/milemarker.postman_collection.json --env-var base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000 (or make postman)

item.name: 1. Demo
New York to Los Angeles: the full plan

exec: pm.test("fewer than 10 stops, and summary.stops matches the list", function () { pm.expect(stops.length).to.be.below(10); pm.expect(s.stops).to.eql(stops.length); });
pm.test("total_fuel_cost equals the sum of the stops' costs, to the cent", function () {

pm.test("first stop is the start", function () { pm.expect(stops[0].kind).to.eql("start"); });
pm.test("lowest_possible_fuel_cost is not above total_fuel_cost", function () { pm.expect(s.lowest_possible_fuel_cost).to.be.at.most(s.total_fuel_cost + 0.005); });
pm.test("meta is consistent (cache_hit means no routing call)", function () {
pm.test("labels are New York, NY and Los Angeles, CA", function () { pm.expect(s.start.label).to.eql("New York, NY"); pm.expect(s.finish.label).to.eql("Los Angeles, CA"); });

pm.test("cache is redis, fallback or memory", function () { pm.expect(body.cache).to.be.oneOf(["redis", "fallback", "memory"]); });
